Lesson information

Level: A2, pre-teens
Dialect: American
Time: 75 minutes

Goal: can follow and give simple directions on a familiar map
Grammar: prepositions of movement
Vocabulary: words related to Christmas atmosphere
Reading: a short factual description of Pepperkakebyen, Bergen
Listening: a toy train driver explains a route inside Gingerbread City
Speaking: an information-gap route game — guiding a train to the correct destination

items.label: Wordlist
src: **Speaking:** an information-gap route game — guiding a train to the correct destination
Wordlist
gingerbread house - a small house made from gingerbread icing - a sweet sugar mixture used to decorate cakes candy cane - a stick-shaped sweet, often red and white
bakery - a shop where people make or sell bread and cakes bridge - a road or railway over a river
tunnel - a long way through a hill or under the ground

A City Made of Gingerbread
In Bergen, a city in Norway, people make a small town every year before Christmas. Its name is Pepperkakebyen. In English, this means Gingerbread City.
People use gingerbread to make the little buildings. Gingerbread is a sweet brown cookie. You can see houses, small trains, cars and boats in the town.
Children and adults help make the city. Schools and other groups make things for it too. Then people put the buildings together in one place.
Visitors come to see the little town. They walk around and look at the buildings. People visit with their family or friends before Christmas.
The houses are very small. People do not live in them! Pepperkakebyen is a show that people can visit.

**A:** Hi! I’m Max. I’m driving the little train in Gingerbread City. Today I have a present for my friend. I need to take it to a secret place. My friend Mia is waiting for me, but I don’t know the way. I’ll call her.
**B:** Start at the station. First, go along the river. The blue water is next to the train tracks. Next, go past the bakery. Don’t stop there! Go straight at the Market sign.
Then go across the bridge. Go straight at the Park sign. After that, go through the tunnel. Look! There’s the gingerbread house. Stop here.
**A:** Thank you for your help!

Ex. 1.3 A Christmas surprise for Max. Read the story. What is Mia’s surprise for Max? Choose one answer
A Christmas Surprise for Max
It’s December. Max is at the train station in Gingerbread City. He gets a message from his friend Mia.
“I have a Christmas surprise for you! First, go along the river. Go past the bakery. Turn left at the Market sign and stop at the market.”
Max follows the directions. At the market, he finds a candy cane and a second message.
“Good job! Now go back to the station. Go along the river and past the bakery again. Go straight at the Market sign. Go across the bridge. Go straight at the Park sign. Then go through the tunnel.”

Max takes his train back to the station. Then he follows the new directions. Max gets on his train. He sees Christmas lights in the town. At the end of the tracks, there is a big gingerbread house. It has white icing on the roof and candy canes by the door.
